questions.q: Choose the correct passive construction: “Who wrote this letter?”
opts: By whom was this letter written?
By whom was written this letter?
By whom this letter was written?
questions.why: Question form: By whom + was + subject + past participle. GPSC-style practice item, modelled on the 2026 grammar blocks.

questions.q: Choose the correct article: “Honesty is ____ best policy.”
questions.why: Fixed proverb: 'the best policy'. GPSC-style practice item.

questions.q: Choose the correct preposition: “She insisted ____ paying the bill herself.”

opts: This hospital is more better equipped than any other hospital in the district.
This hospital is better equipped than any hospital in the district.
This hospital is best equipped than any other hospital in the district.
This hospital is better equipped than any other hospital in the district.
questions.why: Comparing one member with the rest of its own group needs 'any other'. GPSC-style practice item, modelled on the 2026 grammar blocks.

questions.q: Choose the correct tense: “I ____ to Paris twice so far.”
questions.why: 'So far' signals the present perfect. GPSC-style practice item.
GPSC 2024 key: 'benefited' (single t). GPSC-style practice item.

questions.q: Identify the error: “I look forward to meet you at the conference next week.”
questions.why: 'Look forward to' takes a gerund: 'to meeting'. GPSC-style practice item.

questions.q: Choose the correct passive construction: “The authority ordered him to submit the documents.”
opts: He was ordered to submit the documents.
He is ordered to submit the documents.
He was ordered submitting the documents.
To submit the documents was ordered to him.
questions.why: Past active becomes 'was ordered'; the infinitive 'to submit' stays. GPSC CBRT, Sep 2026.

questions.q: Complete the sentence: “Not until the report arrived ____ the matter.”
questions.why: 'Not until' + clause is followed by inversion in the main clause. GPSC-style practice item.

questions.q: Select the correct indirect speech: The doctor said to me, “Take this medicine twice a day.”
opts: The doctor said me to take this medicine twice a day.
The doctor told that I take that medicine twice a day.
The doctor advised me to take that medicine twice a day.
The doctor advised me that take the medicine twice a day.
questions.why: Advice or orders become told/advised + object + to-infinitive; this → that. GPSC-style practice item, modelled on the 2026 grammar blocks.
